questions.stem: Under the international Rule 28, what may a vessel constrained by her draught show in addition to her power-driven lights?
options: Three all-round red lights in a vertical line
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
Red, white, red in a vertical line
questions.explanation: Rule 28(a) allows three all-round reds in a vertical line. Two reds is not under command, red, white, red is restricted in ability to manoeuvre, and three greens is mine clearance.

questions.stem: What day shape may a vessel constrained by her draught show?
questions.explanation: Rule 28 gives a cylinder. A diamond marks a long tow, two balls not under command, and a cone apex upwards outlying fishing gear.

questions.stem: A loaded bulk carrier is berthing in a Canadian harbour on the BC coast. Under the Canadian modification, may she show three all-round red lights in a vertical line to indicate that she is constrained by her draught?
options: Yes, the signal is always allowed for deep-draught vessels
Only if Vessel Traffic Services approves
No, in Canadian waters of a roadstead, harbour, river, lake or inland waterway no vessel may show those lights or a cylinder
questions.explanation: Rule 28(b), a Canadian modification, says no vessel shall show three all-round reds in a vertical line or a cylinder in Canadian waters of a roadstead, harbour, river, lake or inland waterway. There is no daytime or traffic-service exception in the rule.

questions.stem: Which kind of vessel can be a "vessel constrained by her draught" under the Rules?
questions.explanation: Rule 3(h) defines a vessel constrained by her draught as a power-driven vessel whose draught, compared with the available depth and width of navigable water, severely restricts her ability to deviate from her course. No length limit is set, and she is underway, not at anchor.

questions.stem: Outside Canadian waters, your power-driven vessel meets a ship showing three all-round red lights in a vertical line with her masthead lights and sidelights. What do the Rules ask of you?
options: Nothing special; she is only showing an optional signal
Treat her as a vessel not under command and stand on
If the circumstances of the case admit, avoid impeding her safe passage
Stop and wait until she is past, in all cases
questions.explanation: Rule 18(d) asks any vessel other than NUC or RAM to avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draught showing the Rule 28 signals, if circumstances admit. The signal being optional for her does not make it meaningless for you. The Rules do not require you to stop in all cases, and she is not NUC.

questions.stem: Which word in the international Rule 28 tells you that showing the constrained-by-draught signal is the vessel's choice?
questions.explanation: Rule 28(a) says a vessel constrained by her draught "may" show the three reds or a cylinder, so the signal is optional. In Canadian inland waters the Canadian modification goes further and forbids it.
